newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs cheered by Tokyo stock fall, investor bids.
newsitem.headline: JGBs cheered by Tokyo stock fall, investor bids.

text.p: Cash and futures Japanese government bonds (JGBs) rose by midday on Wednesday in response to the weakness in Tokyo stocks and substantial bids from investors, traders said.
Short position holders in the March were being squeezed after it breached the key resistance of 124.80. The March ended the morning session at 124.88, up from 124.71.
There was talk that major public funds, such as the Postal Life Insurance System, known as Kampo, bought long-term JGBs, adding to the bullishness of the market, traders said.
At midday, the Nikkei average was down 282.43 points or 1.42 percent at 19,571.46. Its September futures shed 330 points to 19,590.
Fears of an oversupply of corporate bonds, which depressed bond prices in recent days, appear to have subsided.
The price of Tokyo Electric Power Co's (TEPCO) 2.625 percent bond issued at par on Tuesday stopped falling and stabilised by early trading on Wednesday, traders said.
TEPCO's issue dived to 99.40 a few hours after the launch on Tuesday due to unattractive terms on the issue. It was also traded at 99.40 on Wednesday.
Despite improving corporate bond market conditions, investors remained wary of buying corporate bonds, traders said.

Overnight in London, traders said hedge sales against holding NTT's 100 billion 2.5 percent 10-year bond launched on Tuesday by underwriting brokerages were detected in the JGB futures market on the LIFFE.
The yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB was at 2.300 percent, down from 2.325 percent on Tuesday.
